monogr.title: We propose a new evaluation criterion for word similarity measures, called meaning-entailing substitutability, which is suitable for semantic-oriented NLP applications. This criterion can be assessed independently of any specific application with a high level of human agreement. We examine the quality of distributional word feature vectors and their impact on word similarity results, introducing an objective measure for evaluating the quality of these feature vectors. Additionally, we present a novel feature weighting and selection function that generates superior feature vectors and enhances word similarity performance
